thread:
ben: Hey team — after moving our auth flow to Cloudflare Workers + the edge TypeScript SDK we're seeing sporadic 401s and a couple duplicate billing events. Root cause looks like the Authorization header is missing on the POST after an OPTIONS preflight.

ben: Minimal repro:
```
// edge runtime (Cloudflare)
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  mode: 'cors',
  credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'hello' })
})
```

ben: Logs show an OPTIONS 204, then a POST with no Authorization and a 401 from the Redwood API. When our client retries the request (SDK automatic retry) the second POST sometimes goes through — which is causing unexpected charge counts.

support-bot: Ticket #4201 created and linked to this thread :ticket:

samir: Can you paste the exact edge SDK version and the worker runtime (Cloudflare Workers / Vercel Edge / Deno) please?

ben: Using @redwood/edge-sdk v0.9.4 on Cloudflare Workers (wrangler 3.12). Node bundles on local repro behave fine.

julia: Thanks — this smells like the older edge-sdk fetch-wrapper that mutated headers before the runtime did CORS handling. CF Workers enumerate headers and will drop Authorization on the actual POST if the preflight configuration doesn't match exactly. Two quick asks:
1) can you confirm the preflight request returns Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization ?
2) try sending the header key lower-cased: `authorization` and report back.

ben: Preflight response headers (captured via worker logs):
```
OPTIONS /v1/generate 204
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: content-type
```
ben: As you can see, Authorization is missing from the ACAH list — so browser preflight won't permit the header. But we didn't explicitly set that on our forwarding path — the SDK should preserve incoming headers or set the ACAH when proxying.

samir: Right — a bug we tracked: older edge-sdk versions (<=0.9.x) had a forwarding path that forgot to add Authorization to ACAH when doing an OPTIONS response shim. That + Cloudflare's header canonicalization leads to the header being dropped on the subsequent POST. The auto-retry then ends up resending and sometimes charges apply twice.

samir: Workarounds:
- short-term: explicitly add `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization` on your worker's preflight response.
- alternative: send token in a cookie or in the query string for the edge route (not ideal).
- quick client change: switch to lower-case header name `authorization` (some runtimes preserve it differently), e.g.:
```
headers: {
  authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}`,
  'content-type': 'application/json'
}
```

julia: Long-term fix: upgrade @redwood/edge-sdk to v0.11.0 — release notes: fixes preflight header forwarding and avoids the extra automatic retry when preflight fails. This should stop the Authorization drop and duplicate billing. Release PR: #789 (internal)

ben: I tried the lower-case header workaround and adding ACAH: Authorization to OPTIONS — both stop the 401s. Upgrading is best but the ACAH change is easy to deploy now.

samir: Can you also verify you're not setting `keepalive: true` on the fetch? On some edge runtimes keepalive may change header behavior during OPTIONS/Post sequencing.

ben: We're not using keepalive. Confirmed.

julia: Follow-ups for us:
- eng/runtime to push 0.11.0 to the canary edge image (assigned to @julia)
- devex to add a CORS note in the edge SDK docs about ACAH and Authorization (assigned to @samir)

ben: Thanks — marking this fixed for our app once you cut the release. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

support-bot: Follow-up reminder set for release verification in 48h.
